host: Local Windows 11 host (Git Bash), NOT a GCP instance -- both sponsor instances were deleted on 2026-09-24 and the sponsor account itself was deleted the same day.
how_the_gate_ties_this_record_to_history: verify_paper_claims.py checks that cloned_head is an ancestor of HEAD, that pin_at_clone equals the BUILD_PIN.json blob at cloned_head, and that the clone really ran under core.autocrlf=true with all three text artifacts checked out LF. A record whose digests do not match the commit it claims to describe cannot pass.

pin_at_clone.regenerate: recompile paper/paper.tex, run scripts/extract_pdf_text.py, then scripts/pin_paper_build.py; verify_paper_claims.py compares the four hashes below against the bytes on disk

supersedes.fix: commit 66a9705 replaced the three mtime predicates with sha256 comparison against paper/BUILD_PIN.json, and pinned paper/** as -text in .gitattributes after the same clone showed paper.tex and paper_text.txt checking out CRLF there and LF in the authoring tree.
supersedes.the_single_failure: the PDF is newer than the LaTeX source
supersedes.why_it_failed: mtime comparison. In that clone the four paper artifacts were written within 7 ms of each other and paper.pdf came out 1 ms older than paper.tex. The verdict was decided by checkout write ordering, not by whether the PDF was stale.

what_this_is: The documented verification chain run in a fresh clone of the pushed public branch, on the adversarial configuration that broke it: Windows, core.autocrlf=true, no local state.
